title: Oracle Asks Regulators to Expedite Gas Pipeline for Data Center
source_used: Yahoo Finance copy of Bloomberg (Investing.com read as well)
key_facts: Oracle is renewing its request that federal regulators approve, as quickly as possible, a natural gas pipeline needed to power its data center project in New Mexico (Project Jupiter), Bloomberg reports.
Josh Pitcock, Oracle's senior vice president of government affairs, said in a letter to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) on Tuesday that 'Time remains of the essence'.

The 17.8-mile Green Chile pipeline would carry about 400 million cubic feet of natural gas a day to fuel cells supplied by Bloom Energy to power the site; it is operated by a subsidiary of Energy Transfer LP.

The pipeline has already slipped to February 2027 from an earlier target of 15 Aug, after New Mexico officials rejected the original route through state lands and Energy Transfer rerouted it across federal lands.

FERC's 4 Sept environmental assessment drew pushback from advocacy groups; New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez said FERC must either revise it or issue a full environmental impact statement covering both the data center and the pipeline.
Oracle is considering trucking gas to Bloom's equipment as a stopgap, as it has done on smaller projects in Utah and Texas, but that likely only helps initial commissioning, not full power needs.
Investing.com adds that Oracle's letter cites nearly 5,800 peak construction jobs and up to $1.1 billion in annual economic output for Doña Ana County.
quote_evidence: Oracle Corp. is renewing its request that federal regulators approve a natural gas pipeline needed to power its massive data center project in New Mexico as quickly as possible.
"Time remains of the essence," Josh Pitcock, senior vice president of government affairs at Oracle, said in a letter Tuesday to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.
That's well past an earlier targeted in-service date of Aug. 15.
why_it_matters_hint: Oracle's New Mexico AI campus depends on a gas pipeline whose approval is delayed and contested.
